chen-tianshi.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
chen-tianshi.period: 2016-2017 founding and Series A; US Entity List action in December 2022
chen-tianshi.summary: Cambricon was spun out of a Chinese Academy of Sciences institute and its early financing included state-linked investors; the US later listed Cambricon entities for supporting Chinese military modernization. These are corporate and institutional facts. The review found no evidence about Chen Tianshi personally exercising political leverage or securing a preferential exemption, so no estimate is made.
chen-tianshi.mechanism: State-linked research and investment backing for a chip startup (corporate level)

support.text: Cambricon’s August 2017 Series A was led by SDIC Chuangye, described as a subsidiary of China’s State Development and Investment Corporation, with the CAS investment arm also participating. The company spun off from the CAS Institute of Computing Technology and received US$1.4 million from CAS in April 2017.
support.source: Asian Scientist: Cambricon raises US$100 million
support.kind: Reported state-linked financing of the company
support.access: Page summary reviewed; fetched text was a condensed extraction

support.text: The US Bureau of Industry and Security added Cambricon entities to the Entity List for acquiring and attempting to acquire US-origin items in support of China’s military modernization, describing them as major AI chip R&D, manufacturing and sales entities.
support.kind: Primary regulatory action against corporate entities
support.access: Page text reviewed (extract of Cambricon entries)

counter.text: The Entity List action names companies, not Chen Tianshi, and is a US export-control determination, not a finding of preferential treatment or misconduct by him.
counter.source: Federal Register / GovInfo (scope of the listing)

counter.text: State venture and academy funding of a university spin-out is a common innovation-policy arrangement in China; the article does not allege any improper favor.

chen-tianshi.limitations: Not exoneration. Did not locate documents on his personal political roles, procurement or subsidy terms, or the share-price-driven wealth rise, and Chinese-language sources were not searched exhaustively. Public investors and a state-affiliated institute holding stakes does not by itself show wealth-power feedback.

kwong-siu-hing.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
kwong-siu-hing.summary: Kwong Siu-hing is the matriarch of the family controlling Sun Hung Kai Properties. Her son Thomas Kwok was convicted in 2014 of conspiracy involving misconduct in public office by Hong Kong’s former Chief Secretary; her son Raymond Kwok was acquitted. The reviewed sources do not name Kwong Siu-hing in the case, and no guilt is transferred to her. Evidence about her own conduct was not found.
kwong-siu-hing.mechanism: Family-company executive payments to a senior official (convicted individual: Thomas Kwok, not Kwong Siu-hing)

support.text: On 23 December 2014 the Court of First Instance sentenced former Chief Secretary Rafael Hui to 7.5 years and SHKP co-chairman Thomas Kwok to 5 years (plus fine and director disqualification) in a case of bribery-related conspiracy and misconduct in public office.
support.kind: Primary court-outcome summary regarding a family member
support.access: Page text reviewed; the summary of which defendant was convicted on which count was internally inconsistent

support.text: Wikipedia lists Kwong Siu-hing as SHKP chairman 2008-2011 and, citing The Standard, as controlling shareholder who removed Walter Kwok from his post in 2008; the company is controlled by the Kwok family trust.

counter.text: Raymond Kwok was acquitted of all charges and the ICAC release does not mention Kwong Siu-hing, so the conviction cannot be attributed to her.

kwong-siu-hing.limitations: Not exoneration, and no assessment of her personal conduct. The case concerned a son and a public official; policy influence of the Kwok property business on Hong Kong land policy was not researched here. Forbes entry is for the widow of the founder, not Thomas, Raymond or Walter Kwok.

henry-nicholas-iii.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
henry-nicholas-iii.summary: Henry Nicholas, Broadcom co-founder, faced criminal and SEC stock-option backdating allegations and separate drug charges. The criminal backdating indictment was dismissed with prejudice in December 2009, the drug charges were later dismissed, and the SEC did not pursue its case. Those matters concern corporate-governance and personal-conduct allegations, not a documented wealth-political power exchange; no political-power evidence was found.
henry-nicholas-iii.mechanism: None established (legal allegations were dismissed; not a political mechanism)

support.text: The SEC sued Nicholas and others in May 2008 for allegedly backdating options from 1998 to 2003; the SEC later stated it did not intend to proceed after the criminal indictment against Nicholas was dismissed with prejudice on 15 December 2009 and the court found the evidence likely insufficient.

counter.text: Fox News reported on 28 May 2010 that prosecutors would not appeal dismissal of the backdating and narcotics charges against Nicholas, after Judge Carney criticized prosecutorial misconduct.
counter.source: Fox News: prosecutors will not appeal dismissals

henry-nicholas-iii.limitations: Not exoneration of anything beyond these case outcomes; no pardon claims were verified. Political donations, lobbying or policy influence were not found in this narrow search.

andrey-melnichenko.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
andrey-melnichenko.period: Wealth formation 1990s-2010s; EU listing 2022; General Court ruling 22 January 2025
andrey-melnichenko.summary: Melnichenko, with family, is a fertilizer and coal magnate who was EU-sanctioned in March 2022; the General Court upheld the listing in January 2025 on the basis of his leading role in sectors generating significant revenue for the Russian government and his attendance at a 24 February 2022 meeting with Putin. A sector-based sanction and a meeting attendance do not establish a preferential-benefit exchange; no rubric is assigned.
andrey-melnichenko.mechanism: Sector-based sanctions rationale (not an adjudicated exchange)

support.text: The EU Council listed him on 9 March 2022, citing a 24 February 2022 meeting with Putin and 36 other businesspeople.

In T-271/22 the General Court (22 January 2025) upheld the listing, found he retained economic benefits and influence despite transferring assets to a trust and his wife, and said no personal link to the Russian government need be shown for leading businesspersons in key sectors.
support.source: eucrim: CJEU rulings on restrictive measures
support.access: Page text reviewed (summary report, not the judgment)

counter.text: Melnichenko told Forbes his stakes in EuroChem and SUEK were reduced to zero after the sanctions, and neither company was itself sanctioned at that time. This is his own account; the court found he retained benefits.
The Court’s test did not require proof of a personal link to the government, so the ruling is not a finding of a corrupt exchange or special state treatment.

andrey-melnichenko.limitations: Not exoneration and not a finding of misconduct. Forbes entry covers Melnichenko and family; the court case also concerns his wife’s separate listing, not examined here. The UK EuroChem ruling mentioned in search snippets was not fetched and is not used. Privatization-era wealth formation and Russian state dealings were not reviewed.

andre-esteves.mechanism: Alleged obstruction connected to a senator (allegation; acquitted)

support.source: Bloomberg Law: BTG founder Esteves acquitted

counter.source: Bloomberg Law: BTG founder Esteves acquitted

andre-esteves.limitations: Not exoneration of other conduct. Searches did not review BTG’s relationships with BNDES, pension funds or privatizations, nor any appeal of the acquittal. Brazilian-Portuguese sources appeared in search results but only the Bloomberg Law page was read.

low-tuck-kwong.reviewDepth: Narrow source-led review; not independently editorially reviewed; not exoneration
low-tuck-kwong.summary: Low Tuck Kwong controls Bayan Resources, an Indonesian coal miner. support.source: Reuters via Kitco: Indonesia grants Bayan additional coal quota
support.kind: Dated report of a government decision and transaction timing

counter.text: Energy ministry official Tri Winarno said the approval of the additional quotas has nothing to do with the share purchase agreement; the article does not explicitly link the quota to the force majeure approval.
counter.kind: Official response and explicit limit of the evidence

low-tuck-kwong.limitations: Not exoneration and not a finding of favor. The Haji Isam relationship to the government appears in search snippets only and was not verified from fetched pages (two Engineering News pages were blocked). Prior concession history, the 2022 export ban and any political ties of Low were not documented here.
